message.content: i was asked to write about myself for a flyer ## i was worried people wouldn't come if i was labeled a researcher ## but i’m a storyteller ## i collect stories like data with a soul ## i am a storyteller and a qualitative researcher ## maybe i’m a magic pixie

i’m just a storyteller## i’m a researcher-storyteller## she laughed## it’s not a real job## i’m a researcher-storyteller## i’ll share stories about my research## it changed my life## my professor said things don’t exist if you can’t measure them## i thought he was joking## he was serious## i studied social work## i like order## “lean into discomfort” is bad## i avoid discomfort

I was excited about my career## I wanted to make messy topics clear## I started with connection## Connection gives us purpose## It’s how we’re wired## My boss gave me lots of praise and one area for improvement## People talk about pain when they discuss love## They share stories of exclusion when talking about belonging

shame is the fear of disconnection ## it’s universal and linked to empathy ## talking about it makes it worse ## vulnerability is key to connection but i avoid it ## i tried to fight shame with rules and measurements ## i wanted to understand vulnerability and outsmart it

I was eager but knew it wouldn't go as planned. ## I know a lot about shame. ## It’s about worthiness. ## My research took six years and thousands of stories. ## I learned shame and how it works. ## People with love and belonging believe they’re worthy. ## The biggest obstacle to connection is the fear of not being worthy. ## I studied people who embody worthiness.

I have a supply habit but that’s a different story ## I called my research “whole-hearted” ## These people live from a sense of worthiness ## I analyzed the interviews intensely ## They shared a sense of courage ## Courage means telling your story with your whole heart ## They were kind to themselves ## You need to be authentic for connection

They embraced vulnerability## it made them beautiful## vulnerability was necessary## they were willing to say “i love you”## they were willing to take risks## they were willing to wait for results## they invested in relationships## they thought it was essential## i initially saw it as betrayal## my research focused on control## my mission shifted to vulnerability## it was a breakdown## it was a spiritual awakening

i needed a therapist ## several friends declined to be my therapist ## they said i was too analytical ## i found a therapist named diana ## i brought my list of how the whole-hearted live ## she asked how i was ## i said i was struggling

I found a therapist ##
My first session with her, Evelyn -- i brought my list of how wholehearted people live and sat down ##
She asked how i was ## I said i was fine ##
She asked what was wrong ## I told her i was struggling ##
I have a difficulty with vulnerability ## I know it’s linked to shame and fear, but also joy and connection ## I need help ## I don’t have family problems or childhood issues ## I just need strategies ##
She said it’s neither good nor bad ## It just is ##
I worried it would be awful ## It was, and it wasn’t ## It took a year ## Some people embrace vulnerability easily, but that’s not me ## I avoid those types of people ## It was a long battle for me

It was a tough battle## I lost the battle but gained my life## I researched how people embrace vulnerability## Why is vulnerability so hard for us## Here’s what i learned## We avoid vulnerability by waiting## I asked people about vulnerability on social media## I wanted to understand what vulnerability means## It included asking for help and facing rejection## This is our world## We live in a vulnerable world## We numb vulnerability

we’re deeply in debt and medicated ## you can’t just numb bad feelings like vulnerability or grief ## numbing emotions also numbs joy and happiness ## this creates a harmful cycle of seeking escape with things like beer and muffins ## we need to understand why we numb ourselves

It’s not just about addiction## We create certainty from uncertainty## Faith has become rigid## It’s about being right and wrong## The more afraid we are, the more vulnerable## This is how politics is now## There’s no discussion## Just blame## Blame releases pain## I don’t want this life## We change our bodies with fillers## Hopefully, people will be surprised in 100 years## We obsess over our children

They’re born to face challenges ## We should tell kids they’re imperfect and worthy of love ## That’s how we solve today’s problems ## We ignore the impact of our actions ## Companies need to be honest and fix things ## There’s another way
it’s hard to love fully and be grateful when scared ## to believe we can feel deeply ## to trust we’re worthy ## then we listen and are kind to others and ourselves ## that’s all
